To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the severity of TBI, the severity of injuries, and the neuropsychological functions are the predictors of chronic mental and physical QOL.

the appearance of some post-trauma disorders including agnosic and pragmatic linguistic disorder as well as TCI severity were significantly associated with unfavorable mental QOL, and TBI severity, ISS score and multifocal brain lesions were significantly associated with poor physical QOL.
the severity of TBI, the severity of injury and the severity of neuropsychological sequelae are the predictors of chronic unfavorable QOL in patients with TBI.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the predictors of chronic QOL in TBI and the results may be helpful for clinicians to improve the chronic outcomes in TBI.
the role of neuropsychological functions in predicting the chronic QOL in patients with TBI.
the role of neuropsychological sequels on QOL and it is recommended that the clinicians choose the medical therapeutic priorities to prevent the chronic unfavorable QOL.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a favorable QOL is achievable if clinicians consider the neuropsychological functions of the patients and provide them with a suitable rehabilitation program.

the early and comprehensive care of patients with severe TBI and those who suffer from verbal memory, auditory and semantic acceptability impairments would improve their QOL in the long-term follow-up.
a comprehensive and multidisciplinary care is necessary in TBI patients to prevent chronic unfavorable QOL.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a favorable QOL is possible in patients with severe TBI, but it requires an appropriate therapeutic plan.
early and proper treatment of post traumatic disorders especially verbal and auditory disorders could lead to a favorable mental and physical QOL.
early care of neuropsychological sequels post trauma would be effective in improving QOL in the chronic stage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mental QOL of patients with TBI is more affected than physical QOL.
the neuropsychological sequel of TBI is a significant predictor of chronic QOL.
the appearance of some post-trauma disorders including agnosias, pragmatic linguistic disorder, and psychiatric disorders are predictors of poor mental QOL.
